pr_title: Disable skin selection dropdown while in skin editor
pr_body:
- Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/26829

The ideal solution would be to inform the user that they have unsaved changes, but incorporating such functionality with the rest of the skin editor system turned out to be quite the ordeal (see https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/26829#issuecomment-1925466930).

Instead, as an alternative solution to alleviate potential losses of user efforts, I've gone with [this proposal](https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/26829#issuecomment-1925473251), which is disabling the entire skin bindable flow when the skin editor is open.

Requesting @peppy's review to confirm on this behavioural change (an opinion at least, not necessarily code review). Another alternative solution could be to enforce a save when a skin has been changed, which looks like a simple change as well, potentially simpler than this one.
pr_comments:
One test has failed as a result of this change, but I've worked around it in [the commit above](https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/27013/commits/e67d8b2a8ebcc2093a5da62f20874221c747342b). However, looking at the test scene itself, I wonder whether there's any need for it to exist, as opposed to just adding a test step that reloads a skin editor with a specific skin in mind.

Preview of current test scene:

![CleanShot 2024-02-04 at 13 38 36](https://github.com/ppy/osu/assets/22781491/33b6b3dc-4587-490a-9d5a-b9503db5838a)
sure that sounds better. as mentioned, it was intended to be a simple change. as soon as it balloons to have special cases *just for tests* it's invalid.

issue_context.title: Changing skin while skin editor is open causes changes to be lost
issue_context.body:
### Type

Game behaviour

### Bug description

1. Open skin editor
2. Make a change to current skin
3. Open settings overlay via <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>-<kbd>O</kbd>
4. Change skin
5. Skin will change, user will not be prompted to save. After going back to the original skin after this point, the changes made in point (2) will be lost.

### Screenshots or videos

n/a

### Version

current master

### Logs

n/a
comments: absolute easiest would be just disabling the skin dropdown by taking out a lease on it or something

review_comments:
I *really* don't like this. The mutable skin is required to use the editor... so if this somehow triggers it's going to manifest as a bug.

If we can't guarantee that the skin can be changed, then this solution needs to be reconsidered.

The proposal to disable the dropdown was a throwaway suggestion to begin with, with the idea that it would be very quick and simple to make work, so if even this isn't simple enough to make work well I'd say this PR should be closed at this stage.

> I _really_ don't like this. The mutable skin is required to use the editor... so if this somehow triggers it's going to manifest as a bug.
> 
> If we can't guarantee that the skin can be changed, then this solution needs to be reconsidered.

This specific condition is caused by a specific scenario wherein multiple skin editor instances are loaded at once (which is only a thing in test scenes). I could add an inline comment if that helps.
@peppy I'm also interested in your thoughts about the other solution I proposed (see last paragraph of [OP](https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/27013#issue-2116967038)).
